html:
The United Provinces of the Río de la Plata was the state that grew out of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata after the May Revolution of 1810. It is the forerunner of Argentina. The map shows it in 1815.

Its leaders in Buenos Aires hoped to rule the whole old viceroyalty, but it fell apart. Paraguay went its own way in 1811, Upper Peru stayed in royalist hands, and in the Banda Oriental José Gervasio Artigas led a federal league against Buenos Aires.

The Congress of Tucumán declared independence from Spain on 9 July 1816. José de San Martín then led an army across the Andes in 1817 to free Chile and later Peru, part of the wider independence wars.

At home the provinces fought each other, Buenos Aires against the interior. The Cisplatine War with Brazil, from 1825 to 1828, ended with the birth of Uruguay. By 1831 the provinces had become a loose confederation, soon dominated by Juan Manuel de Rosas.
